en.diagFailRevocationHint: The system curl cannot fetch certificate revocation info (CRL/OCSP, required by Windows Schannel), so the TLS handshake is aborted — this is not a network outage, and npm/git may still work. curl 7.70+ downgrades the check to best-effort, or switch to a network that can reach the revocation service.

en.failAccessDeniedHint: During install, Windows denied pnpm access to a file inside the profile (this shows as os error 5, "Access is denied"; on Node the equivalent codes are EPERM / EACCES). Typical causes: the file or directory is held by another process, the file is marked read-only, the directory permissions are restricted, or a real-time antivirus scan blocked the write. This is the same class of local file-system problem as a locked file (os error 32) — no plugin can be installed into that directory, so it is not a problem with the plugin itself. Fully quit DeepSeek Harness (on Windows, confirm in Task Manager that the process has ended, and temporarily disable real-time antivirus protection if needed), then retry. If it still fails, check whether the profile directory or its files are read-only and run as administrator.
en.failBuildToolchainHint: This plugin depends on a native module that must be compiled on your machine, but no usable build toolchain is available. Install one and retry: on Windows install Visual Studio Build Tools with the "Desktop development with C++" workload; on macOS run xcode-select --install; on Linux install build-essential, python3 and make. If it still fails after the toolchain is installed, report it to the plugin author and ask for a prebuilt package.
en.failDshMissingHint: The dsh command could not be found (it is not on the system PATH), so the installer could not run. Please make sure DeepSeek Harness is installed correctly and dsh is on your PATH (or reinstall it), then retry. This is not a problem with the plugin itself.
en.failedCopyHint: Install failed. Copy the command above and run it manually in your dsh terminal (native build scripts may need manual approval, e.g. pnpm approve-builds)
en.failedDescNoProxy: The plugin catalog could not be loaded (a few MB). The first load can time out on a slow connection — retry, or use "Force refresh" to skip the local cache and download it again. Once it succeeds the catalog is cached for an hour. If it keeps failing, run the network diagnostic.
en.failedDescProxy: The plugin catalog could not be loaded (a few MB). A slow connection, or an unreachable/unstable HTTP proxy in Settings, can make the first load time out — retry, or use "Force refresh" to skip the cache. Once it succeeds the catalog is cached for an hour.
en.failFileLockedHint: During install, pnpm could not replace a file inside the profile because another program is holding it (on Windows this shows as os error 32, "the process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process"). Usually DeepSeek Harness itself or a real-time antivirus scan holds the handle. This is not a problem with the plugin itself — fully quit DeepSeek Harness (on Windows, confirm in Task Manager that the process has ended, and temporarily disable real-time antivirus protection if needed), then retry.
en.failFsUnavailableHint: During install, pnpm could not write files to the local disk — this has nothing to do with which plugin you are installing: any plugin installed into the same directory would fail the same way, so it is not a problem with the plugin itself. Match the error you see: ① Out of space (ENOSPC / no space left on device, os error 112 on Windows) — free up space on the drive that holds the profile and retry. ② Read-only or write-protected volume (EROFS / read-only file system, os error 19 on Windows) — make sure the drive holding the profile directory is writable (external or USB drives, write-protected media, and read-only mounts all trigger this); move the plugin directory to a writable location on the system drive if needed. ③ File handles exhausted (EMFILE / ENFILE / too many open files) — close programs that hold many files open, restart DeepSeek Harness, then retry.
en.failGitMissingHint: The git command could not be found (Git is not installed or not on the system PATH), so GitHub-source plugins cannot be installed. Please install Git (e.g. from git-scm.com/downloads) or add git to your PATH, restart DSH, then retry. This is not a problem with the plugin itself.
en.failHostCliSpawnHint: DSH could not start itself to perform this operation (the system reported that the executable was not found). This usually means the DSH installation folder has been moved or is being updated, or that the profile directory does not exist yet. Restart DSH and retry; if it keeps happening, reinstall DSH. This is not a plugin problem — other plugins would fail the same way.
en.failHostIncompatibleHint:
① Ask the author to extend the supported dsh versions and publish a release (button below).
② Grant an exact-version exemption in the plugin manager of the desktop app (the host warns about crash / data-loss risk).
en.failHostIncompatibleKind: Plugin does not support the DSH version in use
en.failHostIncompatibleReason: The current DSH ({version}) is not in this plugin's compatibility list, so the host refused before installing anything.
en.failHubIssueBig: Report to the Plugin Hub for triage
en.failHubIssueHint: This failure was classified as an environment or Plugin Hub issue (not a plugin-author issue). Open a pre-filled issue on the Plugin Hub repo with this error log.
en.failHubStateHint: The plugin list is out of date or out of sync: the target of this {action} may already be in the list (use "Update" to upgrade), may no longer be in the installed list, or may already be queued. This is not a plugin problem — refresh the page and retry.
en.failIgnoredBuild: This plugin (or one of its dependencies) needs to run build scripts at install time, which pnpm blocks by default via its allowBuilds allowlist — so this operation fails (e.g. native modules like node-pty, or the plugin's own prepare script on git installs). The installer already auto-allows that key and retries once; if it still fails, the build itself is the problem, so no user can install it. Run the install command in a terminal to see the full build error; this is a build/distribution issue of the plugin itself — please report it to the author repository, asking them to ship prebuilt output, a complete npm release, or a prebuilt .tgz.
en.failIssueBig: Report this bug to GitHub — contribute to open source
en.failIssueHint: Open a pre-filled issue on the author repo with this error log (includes catalog links)

en.failMisjudgeLink: Plugin installs fine but got blocked? Report to the Plugin Hub
en.failNetworkHint: The network could not be reached before the {action}: the install source is unreachable (offline, DNS failure, firewall block, or a misconfigured proxy). This is not a problem with the plugin itself — please check your connection, confirm the HTTP proxy in Settings, run a connectivity check under System Diagnostics, then retry.
en.failNetworkRegistryHint: Your npm/pnpm registry is set to {host}, and the package tarball could not be downloaded from it. This usually means a private/internal mirror that has not synced the package (or requires intranet auth) — point the registry back to https://registry.npmjs.org (or make sure this source can serve the package), then retry.
en.failNetworkTarget: Cannot reach {url} — your network connection is down
en.failNpmMissingHint: The npm command could not be found (npm is not installed or not on the system PATH), so a global install cannot run. Please install Node.js (which bundles npm), make sure npm is on your PATH, then retry. This is not a problem with the plugin itself.
en.failNpmTooLow: Your local npm may be too old: npm crashed internally while resolving the plugin's dependencies (a known npm bug — not a plugin issue). Please upgrade npm and retry: npm install -g npm@latest
en.failNpmTooLowV: Your local npm is too old (v{v}): npm crashed internally while resolving the plugin's dependencies (a known npm bug — not a plugin issue). Please upgrade npm and retry: npm install -g npm@latest
en.failOriginRejectedHint: This install request did not pass the marketplace origin check and was rejected by the local service, so the install never started — this is not about the plugin itself. It usually means the marketplace page was not opened from a local address (for example a LAN IP), or the host page origin was not recognized. Reopen the marketplace from localhost and retry; on the desktop app, restart the host once. If it still fails after restarting the host, your dsh-plugin version is incompatible with the host — upgrade the marketplace with dsh plugin --profile {profile} add dsh-plugin@latest, then restart the host again.
en.failPackagingHint: This plugin does not support the official default install method: its git distribution lacks a file the package needs (the entry from `main` / `exports`, an entry its own patch mounts by name, or the patch declared by `dsh.bundle.patch`), so it has not been adapted to the official install flow. Please file an Issue on the author's repo asking for committed build output, a prebuilt release `.tgz` (`releases/download/<tag>/<asset>.tgz`), or a complete npm release.
en.failPluginMissingDepHint: A package this plugin depends on does not exist on the official npm registry (removed, or never published). This is a dependency problem on the plugin author side, not a problem with your environment. Please report it to the plugin repository so the author can fix that dependency or ship it together with the plugin.
en.failPluginMissingDepTarget: {pkg} does not exist on the official npm registry
en.failPnpmLinkedDirMissingHint: pnpm reported that a directory it needs to install from does not exist (ERR_PNPM_LINKED_PKG_DIR_NOT_FOUND): your profile keeps a local dependency (a link: / file: entry, e.g. from `dsh plugin add <local path>`) whose target directory has since been deleted or moved. pnpm hits it every time it resolves profile dependencies, so no plugin can be installed into that profile. This is not a problem with the plugin itself. Remove that local dependency from package.json inside the profile directory (~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>) — along with its entry in pnpm-lock.yaml, or the lockfile itself — or restore the directory to its original path, then retry.
en.failPnpmMissingDepHint: pnpm reported that a package does not exist on the npm registry (ERR_PNPM_FETCH_404): your profile keeps a dependency on a package that was never published, and pnpm hits it every time it resolves dependencies — no plugin can be installed into that profile. This is not a problem with the plugin itself. Remove that dependency from package.json inside the profile directory (~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>) — along with its entry in pnpm-lock.yaml, or the lockfile itself — then retry.
en.failPnpmMissingDepTarget: {pkg} was not found on the npm registry (404)
en.failPnpmMissingHint: The installer found dsh, but pnpm is missing on this machine (dsh uses it to manage profile plugins). Please install pnpm first (e.g. npm install -g pnpm), make sure it is on your PATH, then retry. This is not a problem with the plugin itself.
en.failPnpmPolicyHint: The installer was blocked by pnpm supply-chain security policy — every plugin install would hit the same wall, so this is not a problem with the plugin itself. Two cases: ① "Minimum release age" (ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION): the package was published less than 24 hours ago, and pnpm 11 refuses freshly-published packages for safety. Add minimumReleaseAge: 0 to your pnpm config (pnpm-workspace.yaml) to opt out, or wait until the 24 hours have passed and retry. ② "untrusted origin" (ERR_PNPM_UNTRUSTED_ORIGIN): a dependency source is not trusted by this machine, usually because plugins were previously installed via github: or a non-official npm registry, so the lockfile records an untrusted source. Delete node_modules and pnpm-lock.yaml under the profile directory (see System Logs or ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/hub.log for the full output), then reinstall.
en.failPnpmReleaseAgeHint: The installer was blocked by pnpm supply-chain security policy, and every plugin installed into this profile would hit the same wall — this is not a problem with the plugin itself. The package was published less than 24 hours ago, and pnpm 11 refuses freshly-published packages for safety, so both installs and removals are blocked for this profile in the meantime. Retry after: {time} (i.e. 24 hours after the package was published). If you must install right now, add minimumReleaseAge: 0 to pnpm-workspace.yaml inside the profile directory (~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>) to opt out, but that loosens supply-chain protection for the whole profile.
en.failPnpmStoreHint: pnpm reported an unexpected store location (ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE): the profile directory was previously set up with a different major version of pnpm, and the current pnpm refuses to reuse it — no plugin can be installed into that profile. Delete node_modules and pnpm-lock.yaml under the profile directory (see System Logs or ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/hub.log for the full output), then reinstall. This is not a problem with the plugin itself.
en.failPnpmTarballIntegrityHint: pnpm reported ERR_PNPM_MISSING_TARBALL_INTEGRITY: a tarball entry in the lockfile has no checksum to verify the downloaded package. Read the full log, fully quit DeepSeek Harness, and inspect and back up package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml in the affected profile. Once the dependency sources are verified, rename pnpm-lock.yaml to preserve it, then use the same DSH installer to install a plugin version compatible with the host and regenerate the lockfile. This resolves profile dependencies again: compare the old and new versions, and keep integrity checks enabled.
en.failPnpmTarballMismatchHint: pnpm reported ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_INTEGRITY: a dependency installed from a GitHub branch (for example github:owner/repo#main) changed upstream, so the tarball content no longer matches the checksum stored in pnpm-lock.yaml — and every install into that profile now stops on it. To fix: open ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/pnpm-lock.yaml, remove the entry for that GitHub dependency (or rename the whole lockfile as a backup if unsure which one it is), then reinstall. Long term, pin the dependency to a commit (github:owner/repo#<commit>) so branch updates no longer change its checksum.
en.failPnpmUnusedPatchHint: pnpm reported that some patches were not used (ERR_PNPM_UNUSED_PATCH): your profile still holds a patch entry for an older dsh-plugin version (for example dsh-plugin@1.4.2), while this install resolved a different version, so pnpm aborts the whole install for safety — no plugin can be installed into that profile. This is not a problem with the plugin itself. Remove that dsh-plugin patch entry from pnpm-workspace.yaml (pnpm 11+) or from pnpm.patchedDependencies in package.json (pnpm 10) inside the profile directory (~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>), then retry.
en.failPnpmWorkspaceHint: pnpm refused to add the dependency to the workspace root (ERR_PNPM_ADDING_TO_ROOT): the profile directory is treated as a pnpm workspace root, and this install command did not declare that it operates at the root, so pnpm rejected it outright — no plugin can be installed into that profile. This is not a problem with the plugin itself. Add `ignore-workspace-root-check=true` to the `.npmrc` inside the profile directory (~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>) and retry, or upgrade DeepSeek Harness and try again.
en.failPrepareHint: This plugin failed while running its build scripts during install (the published npm package is incomplete). This is a packaging issue of the plugin itself — please report it to the author repository.
en.failProfileLockHint: DSH timed out waiting for the file lock while writing the plugin list — usually because another DSH process or install task is writing the same profile (sometimes a previous run left the lock behind). Close other dsh windows or running commands, then retry; if it keeps happening, restart DSH once. This is not a plugin problem, and there is no need to repeat the {action}.
en.failReason_accessDenied: The system denied pnpm write access to files inside the profile.
en.failReason_buildToolchainMissing: A dependency of this plugin must be compiled locally, but no usable compiler was found.
en.failReason_dshMissing: The installer needs to call dsh, but it cannot be found on your machine.
en.failReason_fileLocked: pnpm could not replace a file inside the profile because another program is holding it.
en.failReason_fsUnavailable: The disk is full or read-only, or file handles are exhausted.
en.failReason_gitMissing: A dependency of this package needs git, but git cannot be found.
en.failReason_hostCliSpawn: The resolved host entry point would not start, so the install command never ran.
en.failReason_hostIncompatible: The plugin's declared compatibility list does not include the DSH version you are running.
en.failReason_hub: We could not identify this error yet — you can report it to us in one click.
en.failReason_hubState: The locally recorded install state does not match reality, so this operation had no effect.
en.failReason_network: The install could not reach the npm registry or the proxy, so the request never completed.
en.failReason_npmMissing: The install flow needs npm, but it cannot be found.
en.failReason_npmTooOld: The installed npm cannot resolve the dependency tree of this package, so it aborted.
en.failReason_originRejected: The request never reached the install flow: the local service rejected its origin.
en.failReason_pluginMissingDep: A package the plugin depends on does not exist on the official npm registry.
en.failReason_pluginPrepare: The published package is missing files, or its build script failed.
en.failReason_pnpmIgnoredBuild: A plugin dependency has to be compiled on your machine, and pnpm blocks build scripts by default.
en.failReason_pnpmLinkedDirMissing: A link/file dependency points at a directory that no longer exists, so pnpm stalls on it.
en.failReason_pnpmMissing: The installer uses pnpm to add plugins, but pnpm cannot be found.
en.failReason_pnpmMissingDep: The profile keeps a dependency on an unpublished package, which pnpm hits on every resolve.
en.failReason_pnpmPolicy: The version is younger than the minimum release age, or an integrity / trust check failed.
en.failReason_pnpmStore: The profile dependencies were written by a different pnpm major, which the current pnpm does not accept.
en.failReason_pnpmUnusedPatch: The profile keeps a patch for an older dsh-plugin version, so pnpm aborted for safety.
en.failReason_pnpmWorkspace: The profile is treated as a workspace root without a root operation declared, so pnpm aborted.
en.failReason_profileLock: Another dsh process is using this profile right now.
en.failReason_registryAuth: The registry returned 401/403: it needs credentials, or the current network is not allowed.
en.failReason_registryVersionStale: The registry that actually performs the install has not synced this version yet, or the version is mistyped.
en.failReason_timeout: The install exceeded the time limit and was aborted.
en.failRegistryAuthHint: The installer was denied access to the npm registry (HTTP 401/403): that registry requires credentials, or it does not allow the current network/IP. If you are using a company or private registry, configure authentication first (npm login, or write //{host}/:_authToken=… into ~/.npmrc). If you do not need a private registry, point the registry back to the official one (https://registry.npmjs.org), or switch to a public mirror in the hub settings, then retry. This is not a problem with the plugin itself.
en.failRegistryAuthHintNoHost: The installer was denied access to the npm registry (HTTP 401/403): that registry requires credentials, or it does not allow the current network/IP. If you are using a company or private registry, configure authentication first (npm login, or write //<registry>/:_authToken=… into ~/.npmrc). If you do not need a private registry, point the registry back to the official one (https://registry.npmjs.org), or switch to a public mirror in the hub settings, then retry. This is not a problem with the plugin itself.
en.failRegistryMirrorLagHint: pnpm reported that a package does not exist on the npm registry (ERR_PNPM_FETCH_404): that package does exist on the official npm registry, but the npm/pnpm registry (or mirror) configured on your machine has not synced it. Point the npm/pnpm registry back at the official one (https://registry.npmjs.org), or switch to a mirror that has the package, then retry. This is not a problem with the plugin itself.
en.failRegistryVersionStaleHint: pnpm reported that no matching version was found (ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION): the version being installed does not exist in the npm registry that actually performs the install. This usually means the npmRegistry configured in the hub differs from the source in your local ~/.npmrc — the official registry has published it but the mirror has not synced yet (it can take minutes to hours) — or the version number was simply mistyped. This is not a problem with the plugin itself. Align the hub's npmRegistry with your local ~/.npmrc (or the other way round), or explicitly use the official registry (https://registry.npmjs.org) for that one install, or use an offline package, then retry; if the version was published only recently, waiting for the mirror to sync is enough.
en.failTimeoutHint: This operation exceeded the local time limit and was interrupted — but it may well have taken effect already (the installer re-checks the installed list after a timeout). Refresh the page to confirm the current state; if it did not take effect, run the corresponding command in a terminal to see the full output. This is not a plugin problem.
en.failUnclassifiedHint: The {action} failed and the cause could not be identified automatically. This is usually not the plugin itself (it may relate to your local environment or the Plugin Hub). Please report the error to the Plugin Hub so the maintainers can triage it.
en.forceReloadHint: Skip the cached catalog and download it again from the server (use when the cache looks wrong or on a slow network)
en.globalNpmHint: This installs CLI tools globally (npm install -g). They won't appear in Installed and no host restart is needed.
